subproblem.title: Representation estimate for a test form h·θ whose coefficient vanishes off W and on K: |T(hθ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K) (Step 7(b) of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, W, K ⊆ ℝ^P with W open and K compact. Let T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), let μ be a measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (NVector (Eucl P) n) with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ: for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x). Assume μ(W∖K) ≠ ∞. Let θ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n, h : ℝ^P → ℝ and c, c' ∈ ℝ satisfy: |h(x)| ≤ c for every x; h(x) = 0 for every x ∉ W; h(x) = 0 for every x ∈ K; and |ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c' for μ-a.e. x. Then every φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ(x) = h(x)·θ for all x satisfies |T(φ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K), where μ(W∖K) is read as a real number (ENNReal.toReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W K : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ → IsOpen W → IsCompact K → μ (W \ K) ≠ ∞ → ∀ (θ : Covector (Eucl P) n) (h : Eucl P → ℝ) (c c' : ℝ), (∀ x, |h x| ≤ c) → (∀ x, x ∉ W → h x = 0) → (∀ x ∈ K, h x = 0) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |ξ x θ| ≤ c') → ∀ φ : TestFormOn U n, (∀ x, (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = h x • θ) → |T φ| ≤ c * c' * (μ (W \ K)).toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7(b) of the parent proof ("By the representation, T(φ₂) = ∫ g dμ with g(x) := ξ(x)(φ₂(x)) = ω_α(x)(1 − b(π_αx))·ξ(x)(θ_α), and g is μ-integrable. For μ-a.e. x, |g(x)| ≤ c_α c'_α·1_{W∖K}(x) ... Hence |T(φ₂)| ≤ ∫|g| dμ ≤ c_α c'_α·μ(W∖K)"), stated for a general coefficient h. The parent applies it with h := ω_α·(1 − b∘π_α), θ := θ_α, c := c_α, c' := c'_α and φ := φ₂.
Write A := W∖K and D := μ(A).toReal ≥ 0; here μ(A) ≠ ∞.

1. Integral formula. By IsMeasureRepresentation applied to φ, the function g(x) := ξ(x)(φ(x)) is μ-integrable and T(φ) = ∫ g dμ. Since ξ(x) is linear, g(x) = ξ(x)(h(x)·θ) = h(x)·ξ(x)(θ) for every x (map_smul).
2. Sign of c. The space ℝ^P contains 0, so c ≥ |h(0)| ≥ 0.
3. Dominating function. W is open and K is compact, hence closed, so both are Borel and A = W∖K is measurable (IsOpen.measurableSet, IsCompact.isClosed, IsClosed.measurableSet, MeasurableSet.diff). Let G := A.indicator (fun _ => c·c'). Since A is measurable and μ(A) ≠ ∞, G is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const), and ∫ G dμ = μ(A).toReal·(c·c') = c·c'·D (integral_indicator_const).
4. Pointwise domination. Let x satisfy |ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c'; by hypothesis this holds for μ-a.e. x.
 – If x ∈ A, then |g(x)| = |h(x)|·|ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c·|ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c·c' = G(x). The first inequality uses |ξ(x)(θ)| ≥ 0, the second uses c ≥ 0 (Step 2).
 – If x ∉ A, then x ∉ W or x ∈ K. In the first case h(x) = 0 by the hypothesis off W; in the second, h(x) = 0 by the hypothesis on K. Either way g(x) = 0 = G(x).
 Hence |g(x)| ≤ G(x) for μ-a.e. x.
5. Conclusion. By Steps 1, 3 and 4, |T(φ)| = |∫ g dμ| ≤ ∫ G dμ = c·c'·D (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). ∎
No sign assumption on c' is needed: if c' < 0, the a.e. hypothesis makes μ the zero measure and Steps 1–5 apply verbatim.
proof_key_steps: T(φ) = ∫ h(x)·ξ(x)(θ) dμ(x) by the representation and linearity of ξ(x).
c ≥ |h(0)| ≥ 0; A := W∖K is measurable with μ(A) ≠ ∞, so c·c'·1_A is integrable with integral c·c'·μ(A).toReal.
μ-a.e., |h(x)·ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c·c'·1_A(x): on A by the two bounds, off A because h vanishes off W and on K.

audit.reason: All hypotheses match. The proof derives c ≥ 0, constructs an integrable indicator bound on measurable W∖K, checks domination on and off that set, and applies the representation integral estimate. No additional sign assumption on c′ or global finiteness of μ is needed.

subproblem.title: A smooth compactly supported function times a constant covector is a test form in Dⁿ(U) (test-form claims of Steps 6–7 of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f, i.e. smooth of every finite order) with compact support (HasCompactSupport f) and tsupport f ⊆ U, and let θ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n be a fixed n-covector. Then there is a test form φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) (φ : TestFormOn U n) with φ(x) = f(x)·θ for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (θ : Covector (Eucl P) n), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → ∃ φ : TestFormOn U n, ∀ x, (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = f x • θ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the test-form claims of the parent proof, namely Step 6 ("The form ζ_α(x) := ω_α(x)·θ_α is a test form in Dⁿ(U)") and Step 7 ("φ₁ is C^∞ with tsupport φ₁ ⊆ tsupport ω_α ⊆ W ⊆ U"). Both are instances: f := ω_α, respectively f := ω_α·(b∘π_α), and θ := θ_α.
Recall that TestFormOn U n is the real submodule testFormOnSubmodule U n of DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n = (Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n). Its members ψ satisfy IsTestForm ψ, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ (∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) and HasCompactSupport ψ, and also tsupport ψ ⊆ U.

1. Candidate. Define ψ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n by ψ(x) := f(x)·θ.
2. Smoothness. ψ is the pointwise scalar product of the C^∞ function f and the constant, hence C^∞, map x ↦ θ. Scalar multiplication ℝ × Covector (Eucl P) n → Covector (Eucl P) n is continuous bilinear, so ψ is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const).
3. Support. If f(x) = 0 then ψ(x) = 0. So support ψ ⊆ support f and tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport f (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
4. Compact support. tsupport ψ is a closed subset of the compact set tsupport f, hence compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport ψ (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
5. Domain. By Step 3 and the hypothesis, tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ U.
6. Conclusion. By Steps 2, 4 and 5, ψ ∈ testFormOnSubmodule U n. Let φ ∈ TestFormOn U n be ψ together with this membership proof. Then (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)(x) = ψ(x) = f(x)·θ for every x, by definition. ∎
proof_key_steps: ψ(x) := f(x)·θ is C^∞ as the scalar product of a C^∞ function and a constant map.
support ψ ⊆ support f, so tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ U and ψ has compact support.
Hence ψ lies in the submodule TestFormOn U n, and it has the required values.

audit.reason: The explicit construction f(x)•θ has the required smoothness, compact support and support inclusion. These establish membership in TestFormOn for arbitrary U, with no unstated openness assumption.

subproblem.title: Evaluation bound for a covector at any tuple: |φ(v)| ≤ (Σ_β |dx^β(v)|)·|φ| (Step 4(a) of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let φ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n be an n-covector on ℝ^P and let v : Fin n → Eucl P be an n-tuple of vectors of ℝ^P. Then |φ(v)| ≤ (Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} |dx^β(v)|)·|φ|. Here I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P is the finite type of order embeddings Fin n ↪o Fin P, dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)), and |φ| := covectorEuclideanNorm φ is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (φ : Covector (Eucl P) n) (v : Fin n → Eucl P), |φ v| ≤ (∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, |wedgeCovectors n (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.proj (β j) : Eucl P →L[ℝ] ℝ)) v|) * covectorEuclideanNorm φ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4(a) of the parent proof ("If |φ| ≤ 1 then |φ(e^Q_α)| ≤ c_α. By Step 2 with Q = id, φ(e^Q_α) = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β(e^Q_α), and |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ| ≤ 1 by Step 3"), with the tuple e^Q_α replaced by an arbitrary tuple v and the bound 1 replaced by |φ|. The parent uses it with v := e^Q_α = (Q^{−1}e_{α(0)}, …, Q^{−1}e_{α(m)}) and |ω(x)| ≤ 1, which gives |ω(x)(e^Q_α)| ≤ c_α·|ω(x)| ≤ c_α with c_α = Σ_β |dx^β(e^Q_α)|.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, φ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate φ β = φ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}), dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)), |φ| := covectorEuclideanNorm φ.

1. Expansion. By the child theorem std_expansion (cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge, a dependency of this child) applied to φ, φ = Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} φ(e_β)·dx^β as continuous alternating maps. This is Step 2 of the parent proof with Q = id.
2. Evaluation at v. Evaluation at the fixed tuple v commutes with finite sums and scalar multiples of continuous alternating maps: (Σ_β f_β)(v) = Σ_β f_β(v) and (t·f)(v) = t·f(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply). Evaluating the identity of Step 1 at v (rewrite only the left-hand occurrence of φ) gives φ(v) = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β(v).
3. Triangle inequality. |φ(v)| ≤ Σ_β |φ(e_β)·dx^β(v)| = Σ_β |φ(e_β)|·|dx^β(v)| (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, abs_mul).
4. Coordinate bound. By the child theorem coord_bound (cmb_rb_abs_euclideanCovectorCoordinate_le, a dependency of this child), |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ| for every β ∈ I(n,P); this is Step 3 of the parent proof. Since |dx^β(v)| ≥ 0, each term satisfies |φ(e_β)|·|dx^β(v)| ≤ |φ|·|dx^β(v)|.
5. Summation. Summing Step 4 over β and combining with Step 3: |φ(v)| ≤ Σ_β |φ|·|dx^β(v)| = |φ|·Σ_β |dx^β(v)| = (Σ_β |dx^β(v)|)·|φ| (Finset.mul_sum, commutativity of multiplication). ∎
If I(n,P) = ∅ (n > P), Step 1 gives φ = 0, both sides are 0, and the steps above apply verbatim.
proof_key_steps: Expand φ = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β (std_expansion) and evaluate at v: φ(v) = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β(v).
coord_bound gives |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ| for each β; factor |φ| out of the sum.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean agree for arbitrary tuples. Evaluation of std_expansion, the triangle inequality and coord_bound yield the stated finite constant. Both dependencies are necessary inputs in the supplied proof and correctly directed.

subproblem.title: Pairing bound for a normalized n-vector: Σ_β w(dx^β)² = 1 implies |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)| (Step 4(b) of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) n be an n-vector on ℝ^P (a continuous linear functional on Covector (Eucl P) n) and let θ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n be an n-covector. Assume Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} w(dx^β)² = 1, where I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P, dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)) and w(dx^β) = euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β. Then |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} |θ(e_β)|, where θ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β = θ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}) and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n) (θ : Covector (Eucl P) n), ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, (euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β) ^ 2 = 1 → |w θ| ≤ ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, |euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4(b) of the parent proof ("By Step 2 with Q = id, θ_α = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·dx^β, so ξ(x)(θ_α) = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·ξ(x)(dx^β) by linearity of ξ(x). At every x with Σ_β ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1 ... each |ξ(x)(dx^β)| ≤ 1, so |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α"), stated at a single point. The parent applies it with w := ξ(x) and θ := θ_α at every x where Σ_β ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1, which holds for μ-a.e. x; this gives |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α = Σ_β |θ_α(e_β)| for μ-a.e. x.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, θ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β = θ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}), dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. Unit coordinates. By definition, euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β = w(dx^β). Fix β ∈ I(n,P). All summands of Σ_γ w(dx^γ)² are squares, hence ≥ 0, so w(dx^β)² ≤ Σ_γ w(dx^γ)² = 1 (Finset.single_le_sum over Finset.univ). Hence |w(dx^β)| ≤ 1, because for real t, t² ≤ 1 iff |t| ≤ 1 (sq_le_one_iff_abs_le_one).
2. Expansion. By the child theorem std_expansion (cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge, a dependency of this child) applied to θ, θ = Σ_β θ(e_β)·dx^β. This is Step 2 of the parent proof with Q = id.
3. Linearity. w is a linear map on covectors, so applying it to Step 2 (rewrite only the occurrence of θ inside w(θ)) gives w(θ) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·w(dx^β) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β (map_sum, map_smul).
4. Estimate. By the triangle inequality and Step 1, |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|·|w(dx^β)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|·1 = Σ_β |θ(e_β)|, using |θ(e_β)| ≥ 0 (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, abs_mul, mul_le_of_le_one_right). ∎
If I(n,P) = ∅, the hypothesis reads 0 = 1 and the statement holds vacuously.
proof_key_steps: Each |w(dx^β)| ≤ 1, since w(dx^β)² is one nonnegative summand of a sum equal to 1.
Expand θ = Σ_β θ(e_β)·dx^β (std_expansion) and apply the linear map w: w(θ) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·w(dx^β).

audit.reason: Normalization bounds each vector coordinate by one. Applying the linear functional to std_expansion and estimating the finite sum proves the exact conclusion, including the vacuous empty-index case.

subproblem.title: Cut-off estimate for f·L^*(dy¹∧…∧dyⁿ) given the pullback bound (H1) and cut-offs (H2) with b = 1 on L(K): |T(f·θ_L)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K) (Step 7 of the parent proof; Simon 6, proof of Lemma 2.36, display (2))
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, and U, W, K ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, W ⊆ U and K compact. Let T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), μ a measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ (for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x)), and assume μ(W∖K) ≠ ∞. Let L : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be a continuous linear map and θ_L := wedgeCovectors n (fun i => y^i∘L) ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n, where y^i = EuclideanSpace.proj i are the coordinate functions on ℝⁿ. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ W, and let c, c' ∈ ℝ with |f(x)| ≤ c for every x and |ξ(x)(θ_L)| ≤ c' for μ-a.e. x. Write 𝓛ⁿ for Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ. Assume (H1): there is C ∈ ℝ such that |T(φ)| ≤ C·M·(𝓛ⁿ(tsupport a))^{1/n} for every C^∞ compactly supported a : ℝⁿ → ℝ, every M ∈ ℝ with |a(y)| ≤ M for all y, and every φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ(x) = (f(x)·a(L(x)))·θ_L for all x; here 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport a) is read as a real number (toReal) and 1/n = 1/((m : ℝ) + 1). Assume (H2): for every δ > 0 there is a C^∞ compactly supported b : ℝⁿ → ℝ with 0 ≤ b(y) ≤ 1 for all y, b(y) = 1 for all y ∈ L(K), and 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ (as a real number). Then every ζ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with ζ(x) = f(x)·θ_L for all x satisfies |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K), with μ(W∖K) read as a real number (toReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U W K : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → IsCompact K → μ (W \ K) ≠ ∞ → ∀ (L : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl (m + 1)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (c c' : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ W → (∀ x, |f x| ≤ c) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |ξ x (wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp L))| ≤ c') → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → ∀ M : ℝ, (∀ y, |a y| ≤ M) → ∀ φ : TestFormOn U (m + 1), (∀ x, (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = (f x * a (L x)) • wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp L)) → |T φ| ≤ C * M * ((volume (tsupport a)).toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1))) → (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ b : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) b ∧ HasCompactSupport b ∧ (∀ y, 0 ≤ b y ∧ b y ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ y ∈ L '' K, b y = 1) ∧ ((volume : Measure (Eucl (m + 1))) (tsupport b)).toReal ≤ δ) → ∀ ζ : TestFormOn U (m + 1), (∀ x, (ζ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = f x • wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp L)) → |T ζ| ≤ c * c' * (μ (W \ K)).toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 2.36, display (2)) for one index α. The parent applies it with L := π_α, f := ω_α, c := c_α, c' := c'_α and ζ := ζ_α. In the parent, (H1) is the conclusion of pullback_top_form_bound applied to T, W, f and L (it replaces Remark 2.35), and (H2) is the conclusion of null_compact_cutoff applied to the compact 𝓛ⁿ-null set F := L(K). Those two theorems are dependencies of the parent node, not of this child: here they enter only as the hypotheses (H1) and (H2). This child's own dependencies are the child theorems scalar_test_form and remainder_bound.
Write θ := θ_L = wedgeCovectors n (fun i => y^i∘L), n = m + 1, and D := μ(W∖K).toReal ≥ 0.

1. Reduction. Fix C as in (H1). It suffices to show |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·D + ε for every ε > 0; then |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·D (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). This is the parent's "letting δ ↓ 0".
2. Choice of δ and of the cut-off. Fix ε > 0. Put A := |C| + 1 > 0 and δ := (ε/A)ⁿ > 0. By (H2), choose b : ℝⁿ → ℝ, C^∞ with compact support, with 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, b = 1 on L(K) and 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ.
3. The form φ₁. Let g(x) := f(x)·b(L(x)). The map b∘L is C^∞, being the composition of the C^∞ map b with the continuous linear map L; a product of C^∞ functions is C^∞ (ContDiff.mul, ContDiff.comp, ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff). Since g(x) = 0 whenever f(x) = 0, g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mul_right) and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ W ⊆ U (tsupport_mul_subset_left). By the child theorem scalar_test_form (a dependency of this child) there is φ₁ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ₁(x) = (f(x)·b(L(x)))·θ for every x.
4. The φ₁-term is small. Since 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, |b(y)| ≤ 1 for every y. Apply (H1) with a := b, M := 1 and φ := φ₁: |T(φ₁)| ≤ C·1·v, where v := (𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b))^{1/n} ≥ 0 (a real power of a nonnegative real). As 0 ≤ 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ and t ↦ t^{1/n} is monotone on [0, ∞) (Real.rpow_le_rpow, exponent 1/n ≥ 0), we get v ≤ δ^{1/n} = ((ε/A)ⁿ)^{1/n} = ε/A. Here 1/((m : ℝ) + 1) = ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ and ε/A ≥ 0 (Real.pow_rpow_inv_natCast). Therefore |T(φ₁)| ≤ C·v ≤ |C|·v ≤ |C|·ε/A ≤ ε, since v ≥ 0 and |C| ≤ A.
5. The form φ₂. Let φ₂ := ζ − φ₁ ∈ Dⁿ(U); Dⁿ(U) is a submodule. For every x, φ₂(x) = f(x)·θ − (f(x)·b(L(x)))·θ = h(x)·θ with h(x) := f(x)·(1 − b(L(x))); evaluate both covectors at an arbitrary tuple and use ring arithmetic.
6. Properties of h.
 (i) |h(x)| = |f(x)|·|1 − b(L(x))| ≤ |f(x)| ≤ c, since 0 ≤ 1 − b(L(x)) ≤ 1.
 (ii) If x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport f because tsupport f ⊆ W. So f(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and h(x) = 0. This is the parent's "if x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport ω_α, so ω_α(x) = 0".
 (iii) If x ∈ K, then L(x) ∈ L(K), so b(L(x)) = 1 and h(x) = 0. This is the parent's "if x ∈ K, then π_αx ∈ F_α, so b(π_αx) = 1".
7. The φ₂-term. Apply the child theorem remainder_bound (a dependency of this child) to U, W, K, T, μ, ξ (representation, W open, K compact, μ(W∖K) ≠ ∞), to θ, h, c, c' (Step 6 and the hypothesis |ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c' for μ-a.e. x), and to φ := φ₂ (Step 5). It gives |T(φ₂)| ≤ c·c'·D.
8. Combination. ζ = φ₁ + φ₂ in Dⁿ(U), so T(ζ) = T(φ₁) + T(φ₂) by linearity of T. By Steps 4 and 7, |T(ζ)| ≤ |T(φ₁)| + |T(φ₂)| ≤ ε + c·c'·D. By Step 1, |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·D. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix C from (H1). For ε > 0 put δ := (ε/(|C|+1))ⁿ and take a cut-off b from (H2) (b = 1 on L(K), 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ).
scalar_test_form gives φ₁ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ₁ = (f·(b∘L))·θ_L. (H1) with a = b and M = 1 gives |T(φ₁)| ≤ |C|·δ^{1/n} ≤ ε.
φ₂ := ζ − φ₁ = (f·(1 − b∘L))·θ_L. Its coefficient is bounded by c and vanishes off W and on K.
remainder_bound gives |T(φ₂)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K). Adding gives |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K) + ε; let ε ↓ 0.

audit.reason: H1 and H2 are explicit, non-circular hypotheses matching the parent’s sibling outputs. The cutoff choice δ=(ε/(|C|+1))^(m+1), test-form construction, remainder estimate and ε-limit prove the exact conclusion. Positivity of m+1 and all support and sign conditions are addressed.
